answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. Each identity starts with a zephyr-thin score, and only completed work raises it. The core kernel of the rule: payouts scale with score, so fresh clones earn near zero until they build history. An attacker must fund and operate many identities through full work cycles before any becomes profitable. Honest agents reach useful earnings in one cycle, making one persistent identity cheaper than a violet swarm of unproven clones.
